cls: Inhalational (volatile) general anesthetic - halogenated methyl isopropyl ether
quick: Titrated by vaporizer; maintenance MAC ~2.6% in adults (with O2)
Fasting per anesthesia/NPO guidelines before surgery
Use only if clearly needed; uterine relaxant, neonatal CNS data
Brief exposure; resume breastfeeding once recovered/alert
Caution at low flows (Compound A); avoid prolonged low-flow
Caution in hepatic impairment; rare hepatotoxicity
Continuous vital signs, ETCO2, temperature, end-tidal agent
summary: Sevoflurane is a halogenated volatile general anesthetic used for inhalational induction and maintenance of general anesthesia in adults and children. Its low pungency and rapid onset/offset make it ideal for mask induction, especially in pediatrics. It must be delivered with a calibrated vaporizer by personnel trained in general anesthesia. Key risks are malignant hyperthermia in susceptible patients, and degradation to Compound A with desiccated CO2 absorbents and low fresh-gas flows (renal concern).
indications: Induction of general anesthesia in adult and pediatric patients
Maintenance of general anesthesia in adult and pediatric patients for inpatient and outpatient surgery

dosage.d: Inhaled concentrations up to 5% with O2 or O2/N2O, titrated to effect
Typically 0.5-3% with or without nitrous oxide; MAC ~2.6% in O2 (decreases with age)
dosage.n: MAC lowered by N2O, opioids, age, premedication

dosage.d: Titrated; MAC higher in children (e.g., ~2.5-3.3%, age-dependent), up to ~2.5% in infants
dosage.n: MAC reduced when combined with nitrous oxide

admin: Administer only via a vaporizer calibrated specifically for sevoflurane by trained anesthesia personnel
Maintain immediate availability of airway, ventilation, oxygen, and resuscitation equipment
Use adequate fresh gas flow and replace CO2 absorbent if desiccation is suspected (Compound A / exothermic reaction risk)
Titrate concentration individually to patient response; level of anesthesia can change rapidly
moa: Sevoflurane produces dose-dependent general anesthesia. Like other volatile anesthetics it acts predominantly by enhancing inhibitory GABA-A receptor activity and modulating other ion channels (including glycine and two-pore potassium channels) in the CNS, producing unconsciousness, amnesia, and immobility. Potency is expressed as minimum alveolar concentration (MAC).

absolute: Known or suspected genetic susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia
Known sensitivity to sevoflurane or other halogenated inhalational anesthetics
relative: Renal impairment (risk from Compound A at low flows)
Hepatic impairment / history of anesthetic-associated hepatitis
Conditions where increased intracranial pressure is a concern
monitor: Continuous ECG, blood pressure, oxygen saturation
Renal function with prolonged low-flow anesthesia

preg: No adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal data show reduced fetal weight and concern for neuronal apoptosis with anesthetics during peak brain development. Sevoflurane relaxes the uterus; use only if clearly needed and minimize duration where feasible.
lact: Sevoflurane is eliminated rapidly. Breastfeeding may resume once the mother has recovered sufficiently from anesthesia and is alert; minimal drug is expected to reach milk.
renal: Use cautiously in renal impairment. Sevoflurane interacts with CO2 absorbents to form Compound A, which is nephrotoxic in animals; risk rises with low fresh gas flows (<2 L/min), desiccated absorbent, and prolonged exposure (>2 MAC-hours). Maintain adequate flows.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment. Rare cases of postoperative hepatic dysfunction and hepatitis have been reported with halogenated anesthetics. Avoid in patients with prior anesthetic-related liver injury.

major: Other CNS depressants, opioids, benzodiazepines (deepen anesthesia, reduce MAC, additive respiratory/cardiac depression)
Succinylcholine + sevoflurane in MH-susceptible patients (trigger malignant hyperthermia)
moderate: Beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers (additive hypotension/myocardial depression)
Adrenaline / sympathomimetics (arrhythmia risk, though sevoflurane sensitizes the myocardium less than older agents)
interactions.alcohol: Chronic alcohol use can alter anesthetic requirements
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently raise serum inorganic fluoride; can affect liver enzymes

emergency: Malignant hyperthermia (hyperthermia, rigidity, hypercarbia, tachycardia) - give dantrolene

monitoring: Continuous ECG, blood pressure, pulse oximetry, capnography (ETCO2)
Core body temperature (early sign of malignant hyperthermia)
Depth of anesthesia and neuromuscular status
Renal function with prolonged low-flow anesthesia
counsel: Given by an anesthesiologist; you will breathe the gas through a mask or tube
You may feel drowsy, nauseated, or shivery afterward - this passes
Tell your anesthetist of any family history of malignant hyperthermia or anesthetic problems
Do not drive or make important decisions for 24 hours after anesthesia
Children may be briefly agitated or confused on waking
pk: Very rapid - surgical anesthesia typically within 2 minutes of induction
Alveolar/anesthetic effect rises quickly due to low blood-gas solubility
Rapid washout; minimal metabolism (~3-5% via CYP2E1 to fluoride)
Store at room temperature 15-30 C; keep tightly closed, upright; protect from light
pearls: Contraindicated in malignant hyperthermia susceptibility - have dantrolene immediately available
Reacts with desiccated CO2 absorbents to form Compound A (nephrotoxicity concern in pediatrics and low-flow anesthesia); use fresh absorbent and adequate fresh-gas flow
Low pungency and rapid kinetics make it the agent of choice for inhalational (mask) induction, especially in children
Emergence agitation/delirium is notably common in young children
missed: Not applicable - sevoflurane is administered continuously during anesthesia by an anesthesia provider and is not a self-dosed medication.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive anesthetic depth with profound respiratory and cardiovascular depression. Management: discontinue sevoflurane, maintain a patent airway, give assisted/controlled ventilation with oxygen, and support cardiovascular function. The agent washes out rapidly once stopped.
